summary: Top Traders Unplugged ep. 365 (Sept 2025): Man AHL and Quantica papers on trend manager return dispersion (speed, allocation, alternative markets, carry), Kaminski's style factors and Mahalanobis turbulence, and why 2-3 different CTAs plus diversification beats chasing factors.

coverage.note: Intro; Fed bond trend signals; European political chaos
AirPods banter; hedge fund brand awareness ranking; September CTA update
Fixed income signals, SOFR vs Fed funds, cuts priced
Index performance numbers; Man AHL dynamics of dispersion intro
Four dispersion dimensions; speed and crisis; index constituents
Index investability, style drift, volatility and correlation math; alt markets
Sharpe of index replication; Chapter 11 of Trend Following book
Main driver of dispersion; CTA style factors
Magnitude vs correlation surprises; keep it simple
Gas and power; Sharpe diversification argument
Crowding in alt markets; next research

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: if you look at the trend signals, they haven't moved much. So, I'm kind of thinking that could be a potential catalyst.
claims.claim: US fixed income trend signals had barely moved despite many themes (Fed independence, inflation), so a breakout in bonds could be the next catalyst for trend followers.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: bond yields are very good at reacting to it's uncertainty especially about budgets
claims.claim: Bond yields react strongly to political and budget uncertainty, as with UK and French political chaos.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: Of course, equities, metals continue to do the heavy lifting, I
claims.claim: In September 2025 equities, metals, sugar and oil products supported CTAs; livestock paused; managers disagreed on fixed income direction.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: the market has already decided that we're getting cuts. The biggest shocks are going to be if we get a lot more cuts or if we don't get enough.
claims.claim: With SOFR near 3.4% and fed funds at 4.25-4.5%, rate cuts were priced in, so a trend in bonds needs a surprise relative to pricing (50bp cut or no cut), and the lack of trend reflects anticipation of the Fed.
claims.indicator: SOFR vs fed funds, priced cuts

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: let's not forget what happened last time they caught actually bond yields went up.
claims.claim: Long yields can rise after rate cuts if investors consider cuts insufficient or fear inflation, since futures price future rates, not today's.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: we know that short-term models this year are probably the ones on a vol adjusted basis that are struggling the most.
claims.claim: In 2025 short-term trend models struggled most on a vol-adjusted basis; Trend Barometer was weak because it uses shorter lookbacks.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: how fast you chase trends, which market you include, whether you tilt towards bonds or FX, or whether you sneak in a little bit of carry
claims.claim: Return dispersion among trend managers is explained by design choices (speed, allocation, alternative markets, carry), so dispersion is the fingerprint of each system (Man AHL 'Dynamics of dispersion').

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: Carrie as you know has about a 30 40% correlation with trend.
claims.claim: Carry has about 30-40% correlation with trend, so adding carry smooths performance over different horizons.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: being faster is actually really helpful for really bad environments.
claims.claim: Faster trend following helps most in crises; the industry has shifted to slower products that give less crisis protection, though slow ones did better recently.
claims.direction: favor faster trend for crisis alpha

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: in 2009 just one constituent stood out with a doubledigit positive territory and the rest was kind of more flat to negative
claims.claim: Index dispersion arises from specific constituents (one outlier in 2009; two discretionary managers in 2014 later removed), so understand makeup before concluding about manager risk or replication.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: you don't buy 2007's CTA, you buy 2025 CTA.
claims.claim: CTA indices are not investable and manager style drifts over time, so study aspects (speed, markets) of managers rather than rely on index behavior.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: each of these managers as a random variable. They each have a volatility and mathematically you can think about what the range of differences is going to be.
claims.claim: Dispersion between managers follows mathematically from differences in volatility and correlation among their returns, so theoretical dispersion can be estimated.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: they also demonstrate some outperformance of alternative markets.
claims.claim: Man AHL found outperformance and correlation benefits from alternative markets, though depending on the horizon.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: I'm not surprised that sharp ratios are different because it's a back test, right?
claims.claim: Replicated indices give different Sharpe (about 0.75 backtest vs 0.36 actual) because longer lookbacks did better historically and managers differ, so focus on relative and conditional differences.
claims.indicator: replicated vs actual SG Trend index Sharpe

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: how equal risk outperformed historically in our analysis.
claims.claim: In Kaminski and Greyserman's book chapter 11, equal-risk allocation historically outperformed market-capitalization-weighted allocation, with dispersion driven by equity bias, carry, allocation and speed.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: we did find that 2008 given the size of the moves regardless of you know which type of methodologies you use you had a bigger range
claims.claim: Return dispersion between trend managers is greater in high-volatility years (2008, 2022) simply because moves are bigger.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: you adding at least two maybe three together gets you pretty far in terms of adjusting some of that return dispersion
claims.claim: Combining two or three managers removes much of the return dispersion versus the index, but residual 3-4% (replication 500-600bp slippage) always remains.
claims.direction: hold two to three different CTAs

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: I think any of these particular ones will kind of stick out in a given year depending on what's happening.
claims.claim: No single design factor (speed, allocation, alternative markets, carry) is the main driver; each dominates in different years, e.g. fixed income only in 2019.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: we realized like we're very irritated that there's no benchmark. So we started sort of explaining how you could design a benchmark and then we created style factors similar to equities.
claims.claim: Create style factors for trend (speed, market size, correlated markets) to regress manager returns and explain relative performance as with equity style factors.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: you use the Malhanobis distance to talk about how much movement there is.
claims.claim: A Mahalanobis-distance turbulence metric gives a point-in-time measure of movement across managers, decomposable into magnitude surprise and correlation surprise, without needing a window of data.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: CTAs do not do as well on magnitude surprise days, right?
claims.claim: Magnitude surprises (Brexit, SVB, Black Friday, Liberation Day) hurt CTAs, while correlation surprises mark inflection points where trend signals rotate and drive dispersion.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: pick two or three, at least two or three managers that you like, that you think are a little different
claims.claim: Investors should start simple: pick two or three different CTAs, avoid analysis paralysis, because CTAs are among few alternatives without hidden equity beta and no style factor persists.
claims.direction: hold two to three different CTAs

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: things like credit, gas and power, um more
claims.claim: Quantica compared 50 traditional with 120 alternative markets (credit, gas and power, livestock); sector composition explains recent differences, and alternative markets had extreme outperformance in specific sectors during 2020-22 rather than structurally trending better.
claims.indicator: alternative vs traditional market trend portfolios

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: every asset is an opportunity for trend. I just don't know which one is going to work, right?
claims.claim: A trend follower should include all assets because an asset that never trended (metals, palladium, copper) can start trending.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: I think it was like 40 or 50% of the outperformance came from uh gas and power
claims.claim: Roughly 40-50% of alternative markets' outperformance came from gas and power, tied to the Ukraine shock, which cannot be replicated going forward.
claims.indicator: gas and power contribution to alt-market trend P&L

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: on aggregate the more lowly correlated P&L streams that you can add the little bit higher your sharp is
claims.claim: Adding low-correlation trend P&L streams raises portfolio Sharpe mathematically, and alternative markets add diversification though higher costs reduce their net Sharpe.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: now we actually have maybe too much money tracing these less liquid markets.
claims.claim: Inflows after the alternative-market outperformance may have crowded less-liquid markets and added transaction costs, contributing to recent underperformance; crowding analysis (case study of one market) would test this.
claims.indicator: capacity and crowding of alternative markets

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: I've been thinking a lot about macro and systematic macro and some interesting connections between the two strategies
claims.claim: Systematic macro did better than trend around Liberation Day, motivating research on economic trends versus technical trends.
